topics.title: Comprehension, Composition, Sound System, Grammar, and Translation

subtopics.content: Reading comprehension, essay writing types, phonetics/phonology, word classes/grammatical categories, Edo-English translation
subtopics.objective: Answer comprehension questions on Edo passages[cite: 232]; write 300-word narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue, or letter essays in standard orthography[cite: 233, 234]; classify Edo vowels, consonants, syllabic nasals, tone marks, assimilation, and elision[cite: 234]; identify numerals, word formation, word classes (nouns, verbs, adverbs), phrases, and sentence structures[cite: 234]; translate passages between Edo and English[cite: 232].

sections.sectionTitle: Section B: Literature (Ẹbe Otọẹ), Oral & Written Literature

topics.title: Literary Appreciation, Oral and Written Literature (Prose, Poetry, Drama)

subtopics.content: Literary devices, prescribed oral folktales/poetry/drama, prescribed written Edo novels, poems, and plays
subtopics.objective: Apply basic literary appreciation principles[cite: 232]; analyze prescribed oral literature genres (Okha Edo, etc.)[cite: 234, 237, 239]; critique set written Edo prose texts (such as *Idẹn Nokpokhuo*, *Izelogha*, *Okha Edo*)[cite: 236, 238, 239]; analyze prescribed written poetry selections (*Asikoko Ekharha Oghe Edo*, *Poems in Bini*)[cite: 236, 238, 239]; evaluate set drama texts (*Eseikho*, *Meokpaghare*, *Imaguero*)[cite: 236, 237, 239].

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Culture (Ẹdo Ẹwaen vbe Uwa)

subtopics.content: Makeup/adornments, indoor/outdoor games, pregnancy/naming, home training, traditional foods, non-verbal communication, funerals, inheritance, marriage, occupations, chieftaincy/Obaship, Osanobua/deities beliefs
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional adornments, games, birth/naming rites, foods, and funeral/inheritance customs[cite: 235]; examine Edo marriage customs, traditional occupations, Obaship and chieftaincy governance structures, age-grades, traditional religious beliefs (Osanobua, divinities), and modern economic practices[cite: 235].
